Before

 Smt. Tanti Bai And Others
 Versus
 Munna And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri Harsh Yadav - Advocate for the appellants.
 Shri Mayank Upadhyay - Advocate for the respondent no
 Order

This Misc. Appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been filed by the appellants assailing the impugned award dated 17.09.2024 passed by III Additional, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Khargone (M.P.) in Claim Case No.86/2022, whereby an amount of Rs.15,40,400/- has been awarded to the survivors of the deceased Dinesh Dawar.
2.

entities.text: III Additional, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Khargone
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellants submits that the only dispute with regard to the income of the deceased is in the instant appeal.

The claims Tribunal has taken income as Rs.6,500/- p.m. whereas as per the circular issued under the Minimum Wages Act by the Labour Department of Government of Madhya Pradesh the income of an unskilled labour on the date of incident is Rs.8,800/-.

entities.text: Labour Department of Government of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: On this submission prays for enhancement of the award amount.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:8658 2 MA-8301-2025 3.

Learned counsel for the Insurance Company has opposed the prayer on the ground that the income has been properly assessed by the Claims Tribunal and needs no enhancement and also that the appeal has been filed by delay of 288 days and for that delay the Insurance Company will not be liable to pay the interest on the amount and prays for passing the order accordingly.

4. Heard and considered the rival submissions raised at bar by learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
5.

The Apex Court in the case of Chandra @ Chanda @ Chandraram & Anr. Vs. Mukesh Kumar Yadav reported in (2022) 1 SCC 198 : 2021 SCC OnLine SC 3093 has held that where the income of the deceased is taken on guess work, circular issued under the Minimum Wages Act should be Smt. Tanti Bai vs Munna on 2 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149724063/
1 resorted to.

entities.text: Chandra @ Chanda @ Chandraram & Anr. Vs. Mukesh Kumar Yadav reported in (2022) 1 SCC 198 : 2021 SCC OnLine SC 3093
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accordingly, on the date of accident i.e. on 11.03.2022 income of the deceased is to be taken as Rs.8,800/- considering him as 'Unskilled Labour', whereas the learned Claims Tribunal has taken the income as Rs.6,500/- only.
No other point is under dispute.

Accordingly, the just and proper compensation comes as under:-
Rs.8,800/- per month + Rs.3,520- (40% Future Loss of Prospects) = Rs.12,320/-x 12 = Rs.1,47,840 x Dependency 16 (Multiplier) =Rs.23,65,440/- less Rs.5,91,360/-
(1/4th Personal expenses)= Rs.17,74,080/- Consortium Rs.2,00,000/-
40,000/- x 5 Loss of Estate Rs.15,000/- Funeral Rs.15,000/-
 Expenses  Total: Rs.20,04,080/-
 MACT  Rs.15,40,400/-
 Award:
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:8658 3 MA-8301-2025 Enhanced Rs.4,63,680/-
Amount 6 .

Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case is Rs.20,04,080/-
as against the award of the Tribunal of Rs.15,40,400/-.
Accordingly, the appellants are entitled to an enhanced amount of Rs.4,63,680/- over and above the amount which has been awarded by the Tribunal.
7. Accordingly, the appeal is partly allowed to the extent indicated herein above.
The other terms and conditions of the impugned award including rate of interest and right of recovery of the awarded amount shall remain intact.
Since the appeal has been filed by delay of 288 days and for that delay, the appellants will not be entitled for interest.
(BINOD KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE RJ Smt. Tanti Bai vs Munna on 2 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149724063/
